labels.label: ersthm:ThmNotBlocking
labels.notes: Unmarked. The five witnesses (:633-671) apply ers_theorem_4_82 (NestedCausalities.lean:1305), _of_oneSidedBoundary (LadderLocal.lean:478), _of_sliceRestart (ErsUniqueness.lean:722), _of_globallyHyperbolicOn (:749) and _of_isCauchySurfaceOn_secondCountable (Ers464SecondCountable.lean:636). They use data_4_82: ι = Bool, dom true = ]-1,1[, dom false = ]-1/2,1/2[, cau = timelikeLine, s₀ = 0, i₁ = true. All five accept the same hstep term, so the kernel confirms the shapes coincide. hmax and honesided are exercised: 3/4 separates the domains, and frontier (dom true) ∖ closure {0} = {-1,1} (frontier_dom82_true_diff, :620). Finding (3) verified. ers_theorem_4_82_hstep_of_le (:191) and _iff (:205) are proved as stated. The binders of _iff are exactly those of ers_theorem_4_82_of_sliceRestart less hstep, with the same instances. The argument holds: if dom i ≤ dom i₁, then Aᵢ = connectedComponentIn (dom i) s₀ = dom i, which is open, so frontier Aᵢ ∩ dom i = ∅. 'hstep is equivalent to the conclusion' is a fair summary when qualified, as the REPORT does, by 'given the other binders'. It is not a circularity. The theorem's content is hstep → conclusion. hstep's layer-3 supplier still does real work (building the extension U₃ of the paper's proof, ghd_02_19.tex:1114-1139), but only in the counterfactual case, so no witness can exercise it. It is worth recording as a question to the ladder keeper, not the author. It concerns the shape of the Lean forms (a restart fixed at Aᵢ, where 4.64's ranges over every candidate region), not the paper's mathematics. Quotes match :1101, :1106.

findings.what: 'A witness in the paper's reading needs a plane model' (REPORT: 'a model of dimension ≥ 2') is proved only as a necessary condition, since ℝ is excluded. It is not shown that a plane suffices. With one flat causality for both developments, 1+1 Minkowski gives none either: a connected spacelike curve of ℝ^{1,1} is a graph t = f(x) with |f'| < 1, hence acausal, and Lemma 4.70's argument with T = ∂_t then makes U₁ ∩ U₂ connected. So the roadmap evidence's suggestion (programme/roadmap.toml:1724, 'Minkowski 1+1 with two developments of a slice whose overlap is disconnected') cannot give a paper-reading witness. A plane witness would need a non-flat causality (cones turning along S) or C₂ ≠ C. The paper's own example needs d ≥ 2, i.e. dimension 3. This matters for the closer's question 1 (a plane-model target).
findings.fix: In SCOPE and in question 1, write 'needs a model of dimension ≥ 2 (ℝ is excluded); with one flat causality in 1+1 none exists either, so a plane witness needs a non-flat causality or two causalities; the paper's example is 2+1'.
